chunks.arabic_text: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْقَاسِمِ، الْمُفَسِّرُ، الْأَسْتَرَابَادِيُّ. رَوَى عَنْهُ أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ ابْنُ بَابَوَيْه.

translations.en: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, al-Mufassir, al-Astarabadi. Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh narrated from him.

chunks.arabic_text: ضَعِيفٌ، كَذَّابٌ. رَوَى عَنْهُ تَفْسِيرًا يَرْوِيهِ عَنْ رَجُلَيْنِ مَجْهُولَيْنِ: أَحَدُهُمَا يُعْرَفُ بِيُوسُفَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ، وَالْآخَرُ: عَلِيَّ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَسَارٍ، عَنْ أَبِيهِمَا، عَنْ أَبِي الْحَسَنِ الثَّالِثِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Weak, a liar. He narrated a tafsir from him that he narrated from two unknown men: one of them known as Yusuf ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad, and the other: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Yasar, from their father, from Abu al-Hasan the Third (peace be upon him).

chunks.arabic_text: وَالتَّفْسِيرُ مَوْضُوعٌ عَنْ سَهْلِ الدِّيبَاجِيِّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، بِأَحَادِيثَ مِنْ هَؤُلَاءِ الْمَنَاكِرِ.

translations.en: And the tafsir is fabricated from Sahl al-Dibajji, from his father, with hadiths from these reprobates.

en.summary: This entry from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Ghadha'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* critiques Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi, a narrator known for his *tafsir* transmitted via Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh (the father of the renowned al-Shaykh al-Saduq). The text highlights the chain's weakness due to unknown intermediaries and classifies the work as *mawdu'* (fabricated), noting it incorporates hadiths from other unreliable sources, which reflects the rigorous scrutiny applied to exegetical traditions in Shia scholarship.
en.seo_question: Who is Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Astarabadi in Shia hadith sciences?
